anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Engine-level settings for memory, logging, checkpoints, parallelism, and other runtime limits are mis-tuned relative to hardware capacity, workload profile, or version defaults, causing artificial contention or idle resources.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: Physical table or index pages are corrupted or internally inconsistent, leading to unreliable access paths, checksum failures, and mismatched row counts.

When these two root causes strike simultaneously, the system experiences a dual-layer failure: poorly chosen configuration parameters mask or magnify the effects of underlying page or index corruption. Symptoms include erratic and non-reproducible performance dips, alternating bursts of CPU spin and I/O stalls, repeated plan flips between index and full scans, phantom or missing rows, unexpectedly aggressive checkpoint or autovacuum activity, and a flood of disparate log messages ranging from wait-event warnings to corruption alerts. Recovery operations such as index rebuilds, crash recovery, or replication re-sync may thrash or stall because mis-sized memory pools and log files choke throughput while the engine struggles to read or rewrite damaged pages.

Causally, sub-optimal configuration amplifies the impact of corruption: undersized buffer pools force more frequent page evictions, increasing touch-points with damaged blocks; over-aggressive checkpoint or flush policies surface latent checksum errors sooner and more often; insufficient work-memory or mis-set parallelism slows integrity-check and rebuild tasks, prolonging exposure to bad data. Conversely, the presence of corrupted pages can mislead tuning efforts—skewed statistics and unpredictable plans prompt administrators to adjust parameters in ways that further destabilize workload behavior. The feedback loop between configuration misalignment and structural corruption degrades performance, complicates diagnosis, and heightens risk of data loss across both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
